title: Reflecting Across the y-Axis: y = f(-x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: How does the graph of y=f(-x) compare with the graph of y=f(x)? State the pointwise rule.

steps.title: Interpret the Formula
steps.explanation: To read the new height at x, consult the old function at the opposite input -x.
steps.why: Negation inside the function selects values from the mirrored side of the input axis.

steps.title: Track a Typical Point
steps.explanation: The feature at input a reappears at input -a with the same height.
steps.why: New x = -(old x) because f(-x)=f(a) when -x=a.

steps.title: Describe the Sketch
steps.explanation: The picture is a left-right flip about the vertical axis; a graph with y-axis symmetry (an even function) would look unchanged.
steps.why: Horizontal reflection swaps the left and right halves of the plane.

steps.title: State the Rule
steps.explanation: Every point keeps its height and has its horizontal coordinate negated.
steps.why: This is exactly the definition of reflecting across the y-axis.
